stem: Kavya puts a steel scale and a brass clip from her tray into one group. She says they belong together as metals. She also talks about grouping the chalk and sponge by colour.

parts.text: What common property is she using for the metals group?

options.text: They share material properties of metals.
Each metals group must hold only one object.
Grouping by colour is the only correct grouping for these objects.
Two metals and one chalk piece still make a valid metals group because most are metal.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: She groups the scale and clip together because both are metals — a shared material property.

teacher.key_rationale: The metals group is based on shared material. One-object-only rules, colour-only rules, and mostly-metal groups misuse the classification idea.
